[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines the mandatory traceability requirements for all artifacts produced by AI agent pipelines — specifically the pull requests, commits, and related records that result from autonomous agent execution. It establishes the required cross-reference format connecting agent-produced artifacts to their originating enterprise work items, the mandatory content of agent-produced pull request bodies, the branch protection requirements that agent PRs must satisfy, and the governance controls that prevent agents from bypassing human review. Together, these requirements create an unbroken, auditable chain from business requirement to deployed code for every AI-executed delivery task.
page_texts.5:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#scope]

### Scope

**In scope:**
- Pull requests created by AI agent dispatch pipelines as the output of agent task execution
- The cross-reference format embedded in agent-executable issue specs (REQ-004 of STD-GOV-AI-001) that this standard specifies
- Branch naming conventions for agent-produced branches
- Branch protection requirements that MUST apply to agent-produced PRs
- The pipeline steps that inject traceability metadata into agent-produced artifacts

**Out of scope:**
- Human-authored pull requests not produced by agent pipelines
- Internal artifacts produced by an agent during execution that are not committed to the repository (e.g., in-memory reasoning steps)
- The provenance metadata stored in the Compliance Evidence Store (governed by PTN-GOV-AI-005 — AI Audit Provenance Pattern)
page_texts.6:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory.** All agent dispatch pipelines MUST produce pull requests that meet the traceability requirements of this standard. Agent-produced PRs that do not contain the required traceability block MUST be closed by the pipeline and not submitted for review. Pipelines MUST NOT be granted merge authority — human review and approval is required for every agent-produced PR.
page_texts.7:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

AI-generated code commits are indistinguishable from human-authored commits in version control without explicit traceability metadata. In regulated delivery environments — including HIPAA-adjacent healthcare technology systems — the absence of traceability from a deployed change back to its governing business requirement is a compliance gap. This standard closes that gap for agent-produced artifacts by requiring that every pipeline-created PR contain a structured, machine-readable traceability block and that the enterprise work item cross-reference be validated before the agent fires — not added retroactively.

page_texts.9:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**REQ-001 — Enterprise Work Item Cross-Reference Format**: Every agent-executable issue (per STD-GOV-AI-001 REQ-004) MUST contain an enterprise work item cross-reference in the `## Enterprise Work Item` section using one of the following formats, matching the enterprise work management platform in use:

| Platform | Required Format | Regex Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Azure DevOps | `WI#<numeric-id>` | `WI#[0-9]+` | `WI#4821` |
| GitHub/ADO Cross-link | `AB#<numeric-id>` | `AB#[0-9]+` | `AB#4821` |

Teams MUST document which format they are using in their repository's agent pipeline runbook and configure the validation gate regex to match that format. Mixing formats within a single repository is prohibited.

**REQ-002 — Validation Gate Prerequisite**: The agent dispatch pipeline MUST validate the presence and format of the enterprise work item cross-reference as a hard prerequisite in Stage 1 (Validation) before any agent context assembly or invocation begins. A missing or malformed cross-reference MUST halt the pipeline with a corrective comment and MUST NOT result in agent invocation.

**REQ-003 — Mandatory PR Traceability Block**: Every pull request created by an agent dispatch pipeline MUST contain the following traceability block in the PR body, assembled and injected by the pipeline (not authored by the agent):

```markdown
## Traceability

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Enterprise Work Item** | WI#4821 |
| **Agent Task Issue** | #88 |
| **Agent Type** | implementation |
| **Pipeline Run** | [run-id](run-url) |
| **Generated** | 2026-05-07T14:23:11Z |
| **Model** | (injected at runtime) |
```

All fields are mandatory. The `Enterprise Work Item` and `Agent Task Issue` values are extracted from the validated spec. The `Pipeline Run` field MUST contain a direct link to the pipeline execution log. The `Generated` timestamp MUST be in ISO 8601 UTC format.

**REQ-004 — Branch Naming Convention**: Agent-produced branches MUST follow the naming convention `agent/<issue-number>-<goal-slug>` where `<goal-slug>` is a kebab-case truncation (maximum 40 characters) of the Goal section of the triggering spec. This convention enables auditors and engineers to identify agent-produced branches at a glance in the repository's branch list.

**REQ-005 — Branch Protection Equivalence**: Agent-produced pull requests MUST be subject to identical branch protection rules as human-authored PRs targeting the same base branch. This includes, at minimum: all required status checks (automated tests, security scan, lint), a minimum of one human reviewer approval, and no auto-merge without all checks passing. Agents MUST NOT be granted merge permissions.

**REQ-006 — No Direct Merge Authority**: The agent pipeline service account or bot identity MUST NOT hold repository merge permissions. The pipeline creates the PR; a human merges it. Granting agents merge authority removes the human quality gate that makes autonomous agent delivery safe for production pipelines.

**REQ-007 — Traceability Chain Integrity**: After merge, the complete traceability chain MUST be navigable: from the enterprise work item (in the enterprise work management system) → to the agent task issue → to the agent-produced PR → to the merge commit. Any gap in this chain for a governed work item is a compliance finding.

**REQ-008 — Universal Deliverable Stable-ID**: Every agent-executable work item MUST carry a **stable identifier** for the deliverable it produces, derived deterministically from the governing specification identity (e.g. `<concern>-<feature-slug>[-<layer|screen>]`). The stable-ID is the single identity primitive on which linkage, status transition, deduplication, and execution idempotency (STD-GOV-AI-004) all key. Distinct layers or screens of one capability MUST have distinct **full** stable-IDs; the stable-ID MUST NOT be truncated to a prefix for matching.

**REQ-009 — Built-From Provenance Stamp and Supersedes Chain**: Every agent-produced PR MUST carry, in its traceability block, a **Built-From** stamp binding the implementation to the governing spec version and the merge-commit anchor, of the form `<artifactId>@<semver> @<merge-sha8>[ #<sliceHash>]`. A change to a shipped artifact MUST be delivered **forward-only** — a NEW superseding work item carrying a `Supersedes: #<prior>` reference and its own Built-From stamp — and MUST NOT reopen the completed work item (per ADR-GOV-012). The Supersedes lineage is append-only. When a merge commit is genuinely unrecoverable, the anchor MUST be recorded as `@unresolved` rather than fabricated.

**REQ-010 — Traceability Status Lifecycle (status-on-close)**: The traceability matrix MUST carry a `Status` for every requirement, transitioning `specified → implemented → verified` as its work items reach the corresponding lifecycle state. The pipeline (or the governed reconcile step) MUST transition the status when the paired PR merges and the issue closes; a shipped deliverable MUST NOT remain `specified`. A requirement satisfied across multiple PRs is `implemented` only when all its layers have merged (a completeness judgment), never on the first.

**REQ-011 — Out-of-Band Work-Item Detection**: The pipeline's health/reconcile tooling MUST detect **ungoverned** work items — agent-executable issues created outside the governed export path, or lacking the cross-reference (REQ-001), stable-ID (REQ-008), or Built-From stamp (REQ-009). Such items MUST be flagged for reconciliation rather than silently accepted, so the traceability record does not diverge from the work actually in flight.
page_texts.10:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- **REP-001**: Configure the enterprise work management system to automatically link to the PR using the cross-reference format (e.g., Azure DevOps `AB#` cross-links auto-link the ADO work item to the GitHub PR when the `AB#<id>` string appears in the PR body)
- **REP-002**: Include the PR traceability block in the PR template so that human-authored PRs and agent-authored PRs have visually consistent traceability sections, making audit review easier
- **REP-003**: Archive pipeline execution logs for a minimum of 90 days — the `Pipeline Run` link in the traceability block must resolve to a readable log for that duration
- **REP-004**: Assign the agent pipeline a dedicated service account identity (not a personal access token) so that agent-produced commits and PR actions are identifiable by committer identity in version control history
page_texts.11:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- **PRO-001**: MUST NOT create agent-produced PRs without the full traceability block — PRs missing any traceability field MUST be closed by the pipeline rather than submitted incomplete
- **PRO-002**: MUST NOT grant the agent pipeline service account merge, admin, or protected branch bypass permissions on any repository
- **PRO-003**: MUST NOT retroactively add the enterprise work item cross-reference to an agent task issue after the agent has already executed — the cross-reference must be present before dispatch, not after
- **PRO-004**: MUST NOT merge an agent-produced PR without at least one human reviewer approval — automation-only merges of agent PRs are prohibited regardless of status check results
- **PRO-005**: MUST NOT use force-push on agent-produced branches — all history must be preserved for audit
page_texts.12:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. A team lead may request a temporary exception for a specific PR if the enterprise work management system is unavailable and the task is time-critical; the exception requires post-resolution retroactive documentation of the work item link within 24 hours
2. Requests for permanent exceptions to REQ-005 or REQ-006 (branch protection equivalence and no merge authority) are not approvable — these are non-negotiable security and governance controls; requests indicate a misunderstanding of the requirements and should trigger an architecture consultation

[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#cross-reference-validation-logic]

#### Cross-Reference Validation Logic

The validation gate MUST implement the following cross-reference check:

```python
import re

# Configure per team's enterprise platform (ADO formats only)
ENTERPRISE_XREF_PATTERNS = [
    r'WI#[0-9]+',      # Azure DevOps
    r'AB#[0-9]+',      # GitHub/ADO cross-link
]

def validate_enterprise_xref(issue_body: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """
    Returns (is_valid, matched_reference).
    Searches the ## Enterprise Work Item section only.
    """
    # Extract the Enterprise Work Item section
    section_match = re.search(
        r'## Enterprise Work Item\s*\n(.*?)(?=\n##|\Z)',
        issue_body,
        re.DOTALL
    )
    if not section_match:
        return False, ""

    section_content = section_match.group(1).strip()

    for pattern in ENTERPRISE_XREF_PATTERNS:
        match = re.search(pattern, section_content)
        if match:
            return True, match.group(0)

    return False, ""
```
page_texts.16:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#pr-traceability-block-injection]

#### PR Traceability Block Injection

The pipeline MUST assemble the traceability block from validated metadata, not from agent output. The agent MUST NOT be responsible for producing the traceability section.

```yaml
# Pipeline step: inject-traceability-block
- name: Assemble PR traceability block
  run: |
    XREF=$(extract_xref "${{ steps.validate.outputs.issue_body }}")
    TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    MODEL="${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.model_id }}"
    RUN_URL="${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"

    cat >> pr_body.md << EOF

    ## Traceability

    | Field | Value |
    |---|---|
    | **Enterprise Work Item** | ${XREF} |
    | **Agent Task Issue** | #${{ github.event.issue.number }} |
    | **Agent Type** | ${{ steps.route.outputs.agent_type }} |
    | **Pipeline Run** | [${GITHUB_RUN_ID}](${RUN_URL}) |
    | **Generated** | ${TIMESTAMP} |
    | **Model** | ${MODEL} |
    EOF
```
page_texts.17:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#branch-naming-enforcement]

#### Branch Naming Enforcement

The pipeline MUST enforce the branch naming convention programmatically:

```bash
# Generate branch name from issue number and goal
ISSUE_NUMBER="${{ github.event.issue.number }}"
GOAL_TEXT=$(extract_goal "${{ steps.validate.outputs.issue_body }}")
GOAL_SLUG=$(echo "$GOAL_TEXT" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr ' ' '-' | tr -cd '[:alnum:]-' | cut -c1-40)
BRANCH_NAME="agent/${ISSUE_NUMBER}-${GOAL_SLUG}"
```
page_texts.18:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#service-account-permission-scope]

#### Service Account Permission Scope

The agent pipeline service account MUST be granted the following permissions and no others:

| Permission | Scope | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `contents: write` | Feature branches matching `agent/*` only | Agent must commit to its own branch |
| `pull-requests: write` | Repository | Agent must create PRs |
| `issues: write` | Repository | Pipeline must post comments and apply labels |
| `actions: read` | Repository | Pipeline must read its own run ID for the traceability block |
| `contents: write` on default branch | **DENIED** | Agents do not merge |
| `merge` on any branch | **DENIED** | Agents do not merge |
| `admin` | **DENIED** | No administrative access required |
page_texts.19:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#architecture-constraints]

### Architecture Constraints

- The traceability block MUST be injected by the pipeline, not authored by the agent — agent-generated traceability blocks may be inaccurate or incomplete if the agent misinterprets the traceability format
- The enterprise work item cross-reference MUST be extracted from the validated issue body by the pipeline, not re-entered by the agent in the PR body — the pipeline is the authoritative source of the cross-reference value
- Pipeline execution logs referenced in the traceability block MUST be retained for a minimum of 90 days to ensure the `Pipeline Run` link remains resolvable during compliance review cycles
page_texts.21:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#repository-branch-protection-configuration]

#### Repository Branch Protection Configuration

The following branch protection rules MUST be applied to the default branch (and any other protected branches) and MUST apply equally to agent-produced PRs:

```yaml
# Required branch protection configuration (platform-agnostic representation)
branch_protection:
  target_branch: "main"
  required_status_checks:
    - "test / unit-tests"
    - "test / integration-tests"
    - "security / dependency-scan"
    - "lint / code-quality"
  require_pull_request_reviews:
    required_approving_review_count: 1
    dismiss_stale_reviews: true
    require_code_owner_review: false   # Optional; recommended for regulated components
  restrictions:
    # Agent service account is NOT in the merge-allowed list
    allow_merge_by: ["human-developers", "engineering-leads"]
  enforce_admins: true
  allow_force_pushes: false
  allow_deletions: false
```

[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#phase-1-cross-reference-configuration]

#### Phase 1: Cross-Reference Configuration

1. Document the enterprise work item cross-reference format in use in the repository's agent pipeline runbook (which platform, which format, example)
2. Configure the validation gate regex to match the documented format (using the patterns defined in REQ-001)
3. Test the validation gate with: (a) a valid cross-reference, (b) an absent cross-reference, (c) a malformed cross-reference (wrong format for the platform)
4. Communicate the cross-reference format requirement to all spec authors via the spec authoring guide (companion to STD-GOV-AI-001)
page_texts.25:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#phase-2-pr-traceability-block]

#### Phase 2: PR Traceability Block

1. Implement the traceability block injection step in the dispatch pipeline's Stage 3 (Report) per the Technical Specifications
2. Validate that all six required fields are populated in every test PR created by the pipeline
3. Verify that the enterprise work management system auto-links when the cross-reference appears in the PR body (e.g., Azure DevOps auto-links on `AB#<id>`)
4. Verify that the Pipeline Run link in the traceability block resolves to a readable log
page_texts.26:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#phase-3-access-control-and-branch-protection]

#### Phase 3: Access Control and Branch Protection

1. Create or verify the agent pipeline service account identity with the minimum permission scope defined in the Technical Specifications
2. Verify that branch protection rules on the default branch are configured equivalently for agent-produced PRs (no bypass rules for the service account)
3. Confirm that the service account does NOT have merge permissions by attempting a merge via the service account API credentials — this MUST fail
4. Document the service account identity and permission scope in the repository's security runbook

[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cross-reference format documented | Format is documented in runbook | Review runbook | Runbook content |
| Validation gate enforces cross-reference | Missing WI# halts pipeline | Test with missing WI# | Pipeline run log |
| PR traceability block complete | All 6 fields present in every agent PR | Review 5 agent PRs | PR body screenshots or export |
| Branch naming compliant | All agent branches match `agent/<num>-<slug>` | List branches | Branch list |
| Service account cannot merge | Merge attempt via service account fails | API test | HTTP 403 response log |
| Branch protection equivalent | Agent PRs require same checks as human PRs | Review branch protection config | Protection rule configuration |
| Pipeline log retained 90 days | Traceability block run link resolves after 90 days | Policy check or platform configuration | Retention policy documentation |
page_texts.28:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#testing-requirements]

### Testing Requirements

- **Traceability Block Test**: Create a test agent PR and verify all six traceability block fields are present and correct
- **Cross-Reference Extraction Test**: Verify the pipeline correctly extracts the work item reference from a validated spec (test with each supported format)
- **Merge Permission Test**: Confirm the agent service account cannot merge a PR via API — this MUST return an authorization error
- **Branch Name Test**: Confirm that agent-produced branches follow the naming convention across all routing label types
- **Protection Equivalence Test**: Confirm that a test agent PR without required status checks cannot be merged (same behavior as a human-authored PR in the same state)
page_texts.29:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#documentation-requirements]

### Documentation Requirements

- The enterprise work item cross-reference format MUST be documented in the team's agent pipeline runbook with an example
- The agent service account identity and its permission scope MUST be documented in the repository's security runbook
- Every quarter, a compliance review MUST verify that the traceability chain is intact for all agent-produced PRs merged in that quarter (navigable from enterprise work item → issue → PR → commit)

---
page_texts.32:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#assessment-criteria]

#### Assessment Criteria

- **Cross-Reference Coverage**: 100% of agent-produced PRs merged in the assessment period contain a valid enterprise work item cross-reference in the traceability block
- **Traceability Block Completeness**: 100% of agent-produced PRs contain all six required traceability block fields
- **Human Review Requirement**: 0 agent-produced PRs merged without at least one human reviewer approval
- **Branch Naming Compliance**: 100% of agent-produced branches follow the `agent/<num>-<slug>` naming convention
- **Service Account Permission Scope**: Agent service account holds no merge or admin permissions (verified against access control configuration)
page_texts.33:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#assessment-process]

#### Assessment Process

1. **Quarterly Audit**: Engineering Lead exports all PRs merged in the quarter where the PR creator is the agent service account identity; verifies each meets all five assessment criteria above
2. **Annual Standard Review**: EA Practice reviews whether the cross-reference formats, traceability block fields, or branch naming convention need updating based on platform or organizational changes
3. **Incident-Triggered Review**: Any agent-produced PR merged without a human approval triggers an immediate review of the branch protection configuration
page_texts.34:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#monitoring-requirements]

### Monitoring Requirements

- **Traceability Gap Alert**: Alert when a PR created by the agent service account identity is merged without a traceability block (detectable via PR body content search in CI or repository event webhooks)
- **Human Approval Coverage**: Report on the percentage of agent-produced PRs that received human reviewer approval before merge — target 100%, alert below 100%
- **Cross-Reference Link Validity**: Monthly check that enterprise work item cross-references in merged agent PRs resolve to valid work items in the enterprise system (work items were not deleted post-merge)
page_texts.36:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#exception-categories]

#### Exception Categories

- **Traceability Block Partial**: A pipeline bug caused one or more fields to be missing from the traceability block on a PR that was already merged. Requires: post-merge traceability comment on the PR, engineering runbook update, pipeline bug fix, and documentation of the incident in the enterprise work item.
- **Branch Protection Bypass Request**: A team requests an exception to REQ-005 or REQ-006 (branch protection equivalence, no merge authority). This exception category is NOT approvable — see Prohibited Practices. The request should be redirected to an architecture consultation.
page_texts.37:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#exception-management-process]

#### Exception Management Process

1. Traceability block partial exceptions must be reported to the Engineering Lead within 24 hours of discovery
2. The Engineering Lead documents the exception in the quarterly audit log and reports it to EA Practice
3. EA Practice reviews the pattern across teams quarterly — if three or more partial exceptions occur across different teams in a quarter, the pipeline implementation guidance (PTN-TEC-AI-002) is updated to address the root cause
page_texts.38:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Architecture Practice — maintains the standard, approves format additions, publishes version updates
- **Compliance Monitor**: Engineering Lead per team — runs the quarterly audit, tracks the monitoring metrics, escalates anomalies
- **Governance Body**: Architecture Review Board — reviews systemic compliance failures and approves major standard revisions
- **Security Review**: Information Security — verifies service account permission scope annually and on any access control change

#### Example 1: Compliant Agent-Produced PR

**Context:** `agent:implementation` pipeline executed Issue #88 (WI#4821) successfully

**Compliant PR body traceability block:**

```markdown
## Traceability

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Enterprise Work Item** | WI#4821 |
| **Agent Task Issue** | #88 |
| **Agent Type** | implementation |
| **Pipeline Run** | [20260507-001](https://github.com/org/repo/actions/runs/123456789) |
| **Generated** | 2026-05-07T14:23:11Z |
| **Model** | (injected at runtime by pipeline) |
```

**Branch name:** `agent/88-add-rate-limiting-middleware`

**Compliance evidence:** All six fields present; branch naming compliant; enterprise work item cross-reference matches `WI#[0-9]+` pattern; PR submitted for human review before merge.

[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#example-2-non-compliant-pr--missing-traceability-anti-pattern]

#### Example 2: Non-Compliant PR — Missing Traceability (Anti-Pattern)

**Context:** Pipeline bug omits traceability block injection

**Non-compliant PR body:** *(contains only agent-generated content — no `## Traceability` section)*

**Required remediation:**
1. Engineering Lead notified within 24 hours
2. Post-merge comment added to the PR manually documenting: WI#4821, Issue #88, pipeline run reference, and timestamp
3. Pipeline bug filed and fixed before next dispatch
4. Incident documented in quarterly audit log
page_texts.43:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-003-agent-artifact-traceability-standard.md#example-3-complete-traceability-chain-navigation]

#### Example 3: Complete Traceability Chain Navigation

**Audit scenario:** Auditor asks "Show the business requirement that drove the rate limiting change in commit `a3f9d2b`."

**Navigation chain:**
1. Git log: commit `a3f9d2b` — PR #142 — "Agent: Add rate limiting middleware (#88)"
2. PR #142 body traceability block: Enterprise Work Item `WI#4821`
3. Azure DevOps: Work Item `WI#4821` — "As a platform engineer, I need rate limiting on the API gateway to prevent abuse" — Sprint 14, Owner: Platform Team
4. ADO acceptance criteria: Rate limiting must apply 100 req/min per client IP per the acceptance criteria documented on Work Item WI#4821

**Chain is complete and navigable.** ✅
